title: A Burlesque Translation of Homer
author: Thomas Brydges
seller_comments: In two volumes. The fourth edition improved. Vol.I: 360 pp.+13 engravings h.t. Vol.I: 432 pp.+12 engravings h.t. Printed for G. G. and J. Robinson, London, 1797. --- Three-quarter leather binding. Sensitive hinges at the front, tight binding. Previous owner's name written at the front endpapers, pages clean, without notes or under linings. Foxing on engraving's pages – they do not affect the plates. Faded gilt lettering on spine. The "Burlesque Translation of Homer" by Thomas Brydges (c.1710–1775) is a satirical, bawdy travesty of the first 12 books of the Iliad. It is first published in 1762 but this is the first edition to be illustrated and "improved". Published under the pseudonym "Caustic Barebones", it reimagines Homeric heroes in vulgar, humorous english contexts. Homer's Iliad set to bawdy verse achieved some popularity, and was reprinted several times, the last in 1797. In 1765 Brydges wrote "The Battle of the Genii", a burlesque of John Milton's "Paradise…

title: Rubáiyát
author: Khayyám, Omar
seller_comments: The First and Fourth. Renderings in English Verse by Edward Fitzgerald. With illustrations by Willy Pogány. 25,5x19,5 cm. 171 pp. + 12 colour illustrations h.t. and numerous in-text. Thomas Y. Crowell Company, New York, c.1930. Together, a brochure about Willy Pogany and his work. --- Cloth-bound. Gold lettering and decoration at front cover and spine. Light edgewear. Top edges gilt. Pages bright and clean. All illustrations are present. Born in Szeged of Hungary, Willy Pogany (1882-1955) became one of the most famous illustrators of the golden age of illustration, completing over 150 books. Among them are "A Treasury of Verse for Little Children", "Faust" of Goethe, "The Rubaiyat" of Omar Khayyam, "Gullivers Travels" of Swift, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner" of Coleridge, etc. He is best known for pen and ink drawings of mythology subjects geared towards children.
